_notes.pages: Word-card choice: p1 'This.' and p2 'That.' are exactly their own one-word sentences -- this/that -- per the task brief's own note. p3 ('This is a moth.') introduces the book's title character, 'moth', its first and most natural card. p4 ('That is a moth!') introduces no word that hasn't already been printed by an earlier page (that/is/a/moth all seen on p2-p3) -- rather than force a duplicate 'moth' card (which would collide with p3 and be non-distinct), the leftover word 'is' was carded instead of the weaker article 'a': 'is' is the sentence's actual pivot verb (the word that turns pointing into a claim -- 'that IS a moth'), more decodable and substantive than 'a', and mirrors dp-the-cat-sat's preference for the preposition 'on' and dp-fish-and-chick's preference for 'and'/'on' over bare articles when a page has no fresh content noun. p5 ('This, that... moths!') introduces 'moths', the plural finale word and the book's own comic payoff (the manifest's own page-5 art prompt: 'a whole goofy swarm of identical fuzzy moths filling the frame') -- reserved for its own page, matching how dp-the-cat-sat kept 'tip-top', dp-mud-pup kept 'sit', and dp-the-bell-fell kept 'bonk' on their finale pages. All 5 words (this, that, moth, is, moths) are distinct.

_notes.yesno: 10 items (5 true, 5 false), 5/5 split per the dp-the-cat-sat.json / Jul-30 rollout convention. 5 true items are drawn straight from the book's own 5 pages (imageArt = p1.jpg..p5.jpg), one question per page, each worded to distinguish that page's own picture from the others (single moth close-up / moth far across the frame / single glowing moth / two moths side-by-side comic double-take / whole swarm of moths) rather than reusing one generic template, so a teacher can visually verify book fidelity page-by-page. 5 false items use a consistent 'is the X a moth?' frame on animals that never appear in this book at all -- this reader's entire cast is a single moth character, no other creature ever appears -- via imageWord -> docs/picture-bank/photos/<word>/<word>.jpg (all 5 files verified present on disk before writing this JSON: bee/bee.jpg, fly/fly.jpg, spider/spider.jpg, bird/bird.jpg, worm/worm.jpg). Words were chosen for plausible visual confusability with a moth (small flying/crawling creatures) while remaining unambiguously false, which also makes the item pedagogically sharper than an arbitrary false animal. Per the 2026-07-30 ruling, false-item words are NOT restricted to prior-week vocabulary -- picked for clear falseness relative to this specific book instead.
